overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic June Gloom marine layer pattern overnight, with temperatures holding flat at 62.6°F since at least midnight with zero thermal velocity — indicating a stable, cloud-suppressed overnight. SW winds around 9 mph are reinforcing the marine influence, and the high dewpoint (~57°F) reflects moisture-laden onshore flow. The day is trending cooler than climatological norms for late June, driven entirely by the persistent marine layer.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in tight agreement: ECMWF at 68.3°F, HRRR at 68.9°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — a spread of only ~2°F, which is encouraging for confidence. All three models and the NWS text forecast (high near 69°F) cluster in the 67–69°F range. The intraday bucket model shows an unusually wide/flat distribution with an elevated mode around 76–77°F, which appears to be an artifact given the strong marine signal and tight NWP consensus; the NWP ensemble should be weighted more heavily here.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high will most likely land in the 67–69°F range, consistent with the NWP consensus and NWS text forecast. June Gloom fog burning off by late morning, partly sunny skies in the afternoon, and persistent SW marine flow will cap temperatures well below seasonal heat potential. The active extreme heat warnings (Yuma, El Centro, San Diego deserts) are geographically irrelevant to coastal LA. Confidence is moderately high given tight model agreement; the main downside risk is the fog clearing faster than expected, and the upside risk is the fog lingering all day and keeping the high closer to 65–66°F.
